title: Chapter 35: Shattered Mirror
html:
“Why did everything suddenly go quiet?” He San glanced at Lao Zhao. “Should we take a look?”

“If the enemy doesn’t move, neither do we,” Lao Zhao said shamelessly. “We wait for someone else to scream, then search in the opposite direction. That way we avoid the worst scares.”

“Isn’t that basically sacrificing our classmates?”

“No. It’s honoring their noble sacrifice by using the time they bought us to achieve victory.” Lao Zhao stood behind the much smaller He San, who was nowhere near large enough to serve as the shield Lao Zhao seemed to want.

“How long are we supposed to hide? What if we’re the only two left?” He San looked back suspiciously at his senior.

“We searched the whole second floor and most of the third, so the exit must be on the first. We’re practically at the finish line.” Lao Zhao patted his shoulder. “Stay positive. We can’t surrender at the gates of victory.”

“Even now you can still produce this much nonsense?” He San muttered. He had only been supposed to guide his seniors to New Century Park. Somehow he had ended up trapped inside the Haunted House with them.

“Think about the numbers,” Lao Zhao said, counting on his fingers. “We heard Monkey and Xiao Hui scream, so they’re probably already out. Ignore the mysterious eighth person and there should still be five students inside. The odds are better if we keep waiting.”

“Fine. We’ll do it your way.” He San crouched near the door and peered through the crack. Something in the corridor seemed different. He blinked, looked again, and noticed a worn rag doll lying on the floor.

Was that doll there before? It couldn’t have been. I’ve been watching this corridor for ten minutes.He San rubbed his cheeks and looked again. The doll was still there—but now it seemed closer to the door.

Did it move? Or am I imagining things because I’m nervous?He shook his head and checked once more.

The doll was gone.

That is not reassuring…

…

At a first-floor staff passage, Chen Ge put on the Doctor Skull-Cracker costume after sending Xu Wan to look after the students who had already exited. He would handle the remaining visitors himself.

On Chen Ge’s taller frame, the heavy doctor’s coat, rattling chains, distorted mask, and oversized theatrical prop looked even more imposing than they had on Xu Wan.

They want to turn this into a war of attrition?The chains announced every step he took. The sound was effective but made stealth nearly impossible. After five minutes of searching, he still had not found anyone.

“Boss, I can’t see them on the cameras. They must be hiding inside the rooms, so you’ll have to check.” Xu Wan’s voice came through his earpiece. “We really should install more cameras when we can afford it. There are too many blind spots with only the corridor intersections covered.”

“We’ll worry about that when we have the money.” Chen Ge checked the rooms one by one. Near a corner on the second floor, he noticed a small doll propped beside a closed door.

“Little one, why are you sitting here?” Chen Ge studied the doll, then glanced at the door. “Are you trying to tell me someone is hiding in there?”

He deliberately walked past as though he had noticed nothing, then circled back quietly once he was out of sight.

Keeping low, he peered through the narrow crack beside the door.

…

Inside, He San and Lao Zhao were pressed against the wall with their hands over their mouths.

“The chains stopped. He must have moved on.” Lao Zhao was ghostly pale, but he forced himself to sound calm for He San’s benefit—and his own dignity. “I’m not scared. Think about it: if the actor just came up from the first floor, he probably won’t go straight back. This is our chance.”

He pushed himself upright. “We head downstairs now, while the coast is clear. Xiao San, check the corridor. If he’s gone, we move immediately.”

The logic sounded plausible enough that He San leaned toward the crack. Instead of an empty corridor, however, he found an eye staring directly back at him from the other side.

“What the—!”

He San recoiled so quickly that he nearly fell over. Lao Zhao jumped as well. “What? What did you see?”

The doorknob turned before He San could answer. The door creaked open, revealing the dark silhouette of the Doctor Skull-Cracker costume. Lao Zhao backed away until he was pressed flat against the wall.

“Careful leaning against the wall like that,” Chen Ge said through the mask. “You never know what might be behind it.” He triggered one of the scenario’s theatrical effects.

A hidden panel shifted behind Lao Zhao, revealing the motionless figure built into the wall as part of the set.

That was the last straw. Lao Zhao dropped to the floor, stunned into silence.

“All right. Your session is over. I’ll get you outside.” Before Chen Ge could do more, glass shattered somewhere on the third floor, followed by Brother Feng shouting.

Chen Ge immediately called Xu Wan to collect He San and Lao Zhao, then ran upstairs. He found Brother Feng in one of the rooms, gripping a chair and staring wildly toward the adjoining washroom.

Chen Ge removed his mask and spoke to him until Brother Feng lowered the chair and sank onto the edge of the bed.

“What happened?” Chen Ge moved the chair safely aside. Brother Feng was badly shaken, so Chen Ge kept his voice calm. “Did you see something unusual?”
